prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Spiral-wound polyethersulfone ultrafiltration modules show irreversible fouling quantified at 18% flux loss after 8 hours, with a two-step cleaning sequence (citric acid then sodium hydroxide) restoring 94% of clean-water flux.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07419","field":"abstract","quote":"Irreversible fouling after 8 h was quantified at 18 % flux loss; a two-step cleaning sequence (0.3 % citric acid, then 0.5 % NaOH) restored 94 % of clean-water flux."}]},{"claim":2,"text":"Dead-end filtration fundamentals in edible oil refining include compressible cake theory and the role of filter aids, with industrial filter types and maintenance considerations described for scale-up.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07417","field":"abstract","quote":"Coverage begins with the governing equations for constant-pressure and constant-rate dead-end filtration, including compressible cake theory and the role of filter aids"}]}]}
